category_title: At-risk dyscalculic pupils with core deficits in representing and processing numerosity
student_description: David is an at-risk dyscalculic student who lacks basic number sense and one-to-one correspondence, often guessing quantities or freezing when asked to represent numbers abstractly. He is highly responsive to structured, concrete visual aids like domino cards. Uniquely, he requires physical touch, such as hand-over-hand guidance, which not only helps him physically master counting but also fulfills a deep emotional need to feel valued and motivated.

criteria.rationale: David often looks at the ground or around the room when nervous, so he needs direct verbal and physical cues to focus on the learning materials.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly directs David's visual attention to the concrete materials (e.g., 'Look here at the dots') when he is distracted, pausing, or looking away.

criteria.rationale: Because David lacks one-to-one correspondence and tends to guess quantities, he requires physical pointing paired with verbal counting to build this connection.
criteria.check: The tutor models or physically guides David (e.g., via hand-over-hand touch) to point at each object while simultaneously saying the number out loud.

criteria.rationale: To help David understand that counting is not just a rote sequence, he needs to see that the total quantity remains the same regardless of the counting direction.
criteria.check: The tutor prompts David to count the same set of objects in a different order (e.g., right-to-left instead of left-to-right) to verify that the total is identical.

criteria.rationale: David needs to bridge the gap between the physical act of counting objects and understanding what numerical symbols actually mean.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly connects the final counted quantity of physical objects to its corresponding written numeral.

criteria.rationale: Asking David to represent numbers abstractly without aids (such as using his fingers) overwhelms him and causes him to freeze.
criteria.check: The tutor avoids asking David to represent or calculate quantities without concrete visual supports (like domino cards) actively present.
